```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day paying-customer goal favors A. Its core product (upload, RSS generation, directory distribution, analytics) is commodity work on open standards. B's stated differentiator, filing the country-of-residence return too, is something its own brief calls a materially larger scope than any competitor has tackled. B's strongest competitor openly calls it 'the hard part.'",
    "B has gating regulatory steps with unknown timelines: IRS EFIN application with suitability check, annual e-file software acceptance testing, and pre-launch GDPR counsel review. Its own open questions flag the EFIN timeline and the legality of country-specific tax calls as unresolved. A's regulatory setup is light: a privacy policy review of about 1-2 hours, plus Stripe for billing.",
    "B's payer pays once per filing season, so a 90-day window may miss the buying moment entirely. A is a monthly subscription that can convert at any time.",
    "B carries a heavy liability surface: accurate tax logic across multiple EU jurisdictions plus PFIC/FBAR/FATCA, for a sophisticated and vocal user base. That is a poor fit for one operator running AI agents. A's main risks (low margin, crowding) hurt long-term economics more than they block a first paying customer.",
    "Both markets are crowded on the buildable part: six US-side expat tools versus five or more podcast hosts. B's higher willingness-to-pay anchors ($150-$799) do not offset that its only real wedge is the part that is hardest to ship.",
    "A's Reddit quotes show podcasters actively comparing hosts and complaining about price. That gives a reachable, low-cost community channel for early adopters, although no cost estimate is sourced for it."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The B brief's 'Case for' says Atamatax, built solo, can charge $199-$799 and 'attract customers.' The only cited source is Atamatax's own pricing site. No customer counts, revenue, or user testimony are given, so the claim that a one-person build has been validated is effectively unsourced. It is also the brief's main support for solo feasibility. Even if true, it validates only the crowded US-side product, not the combined US-plus-local differentiator.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Neither brief is strong. A has no clear wedge against entrenched incumbents with free tiers. A's paid-acquisition costs come from an RSS.com blog post about promoting podcasts to listeners, not about acquiring hosting customers, so A's CAC is effectively unsourced. A is also internally inconsistent on competitor count ('at least five' vs 'seven'). B shows sharper pain and higher willingness-to-pay. A wins mainly on feasibility within 90 days and low regulatory friction, not on stronger demand evidence. If B were narrowed to a single country pairing with a known EFIN timeline, the verdict could flip."
}
```
